name: methionine_one_carbon
description: Methionine and one-carbon metabolism. Met is activated to S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the universal methyl donor. After methyl transfer, SAH → homocysteine. Homocysteine is remethylated to Met (methionine synthase, B12 + 5-methyl-THF) or committed to cysteine via transsulfuration (CBS, B6).

references: One-carbon metabolism and methionine cycle — standard nutrition/biochem texts.
Homocysteine, folate, B12 interactions — public health / vascular literature.

nodes.label: Methionine
nodes.notes: Essential AA; also recycled from Hcy.

nodes.label: S-Adenosylmethionine (SAM)
nodes.notes: Universal methyl donor (DNA, proteins, lipids, neurotransmitters).

nodes.label: S-Adenosylhomocysteine (SAH)
nodes.notes: Product after methyl transfer; competitive inhibitor of many methyltransferases.

nodes.label: Homocysteine
nodes.notes: Branch point: remethylation vs transsulfuration. Elevated Hcy = vascular risk marker.

nodes.label: 5-Methyl-THF
nodes.notes: Folate one-carbon form; methyl donor for Met synthase.

nodes.label: Cysteine
nodes.notes: Non-essential if Met + Ser sufficient; GSH precursor.

nodes.label: Serine
nodes.notes: Carbon/N donor into transsulfuration (with Hcy → cystathionine).

edges.notes: Met + ATP → SAM + PPi + Pi. Commits Met to methyl metabolism.
SAM donates methyl → SAH. Huge set of acceptor substrates.
Reversible; high Hcy or adenosine can push back toward SAH.
Remethylation cycle. Folate trap if B12 deficient.
5-methyl-THF methyl group → Hcy → Met; THF released.
Irreversible transsulfuration. Compressed two steps. Serine co-substrate.
Serine provides the carbon skeleton half of cysteine.
